text:
alex: Heads-up: noticed a correctness edge with prefix eviction + long-lived cursors. If a prefix gets soft-evicted while a client holds a cursor, we can end up serving stale KV reads until rehydrate. Thoughts?

maria: Yikes. repro steps?

alex: Steps: 1) client opens a cursor; 2) inactivity + soft-evict frees slab; 3) another request rehydrates a different epoch; cursor still points at old seq -> reads return older state.

lee: So cursor references epoch-local token and we never validate it on read?

alex: Right. We skipped residency/epoch checks for cursor ops to keep latency low.

samir: Proposed fix: attach epoch to cursor and validate on each op. If mismatch return CURSOR_STALE and client must re-open (fast path rehydrate).

maria: That works but adds an extra check on every cursor op. Can we make it cheap: local epoch cache + only validate on Nth op or after eviction events?

alex: Idea: add a prefix-epoch counter (cheap 64-bit). On eviction increment it. Cursor stores epoch; reads do: if (cursor.epoch != prefix.epoch) -> attempt local rehydrate, else proceed. Compare is a single 64-bit compare.

lee: "Single 64-bit compare" is fine perf-wise. Where does multi-node handoff fit? If handoff increments epoch on the new node we need global monotonicity.

samir: Right — make epoch a monotonic pair (node_id, counter) or use a CASed generation token from the ownership service. Must be totally ordered for safety during concurrent handoffs.

maria: Also we should emit metrics: cursor.stale.count and cursor.recovery.latency_ms. And add an opt-in API to pin a prefix for ultra-low-latency cursors (customer pays the memory). :moneybag:

alex: Implementation sketch:
```
struct Cursor { prefix_id; epoch_hi; epoch_lo; ... }
on_cursor_read(cursor) {
  if (cursor.epoch != prefix.epoch) return CURSOR_STALE;
  // fast path read from local slab
}
```

lee: Another idea: grace-window after epoch bump where we still serve for X ms to avoid immediate invalidation for very active cursors. But that risks read-after-write anomalies.

samir: Exactly — grace-window trades correctness for latency. Only acceptable for eventual-consistency clients or behind a safety flag. We should document it clearly.

maria: Action items: alex -> PR for epoch counter + cheap validation + metrics; samir -> spec for monotonic handoff epoch (node_id+counter or ownership token); lee -> design opt-in pin API and cost model. Schedule a 30m follow-up sync after PR.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: add metrics ["cursor.recovery.count","cursor.recovery.latency_ms"], feature flag "prefix.pin.enabled", and a canary to exercise cursor rehydrate path.

alex: Thanks all — I'll file the canary + RFC follow-up and start the PR. :thumbsup:
